tricky_patterns.challenge: C# uses COM interop via embedded interop assemblies with automatic reference counting

rust_mitigation.strategy: Use windows-rs crate with COM interface definitions
rust_mitigation.implementation: Define COM interfaces with #[com_interface] macro, use ComPtr<T> for lifetime management
rust_mitigation.safety: All COM calls are unsafe, wrap in safe abstractions, document lifetime requirements
rust_mitigation.cross_platform: COM is Windows-only; on Linux, create stub implementations that return NotSupported error

tricky_patterns.challenge: Remote COM object creation with COSERVERINFO structure and multi-interface queries

rust_mitigation.implementation: Define MULTI_QI structure, marshal GUID arrays carefully, handle HRESULT errors
rust_mitigation.safety: Unsafe block required, validate server name, handle network failures gracefully

tricky_patterns.pattern: LDAP Binary Attribute Parsing (Security Descriptors, Flags)
tricky_patterns.challenge: Binary LDAP attributes like nTSecurityDescriptor, flags, and time periods need manual parsing

rust_mitigation.strategy: Use ldap3 crate for queries, implement custom binary parsers for attributes
rust_mitigation.implementation: Define parsers for: RawSecurityDescriptor (binary ACL format), flag enums (use bitflags!), time periods (i64 conversion)
rust_mitigation.safety: Validate all byte array bounds, use nom parser combinator for structured parsing
rust_mitigation.cross_platform: LDAP client works cross-platform, but AD-specific attributes are Windows-only

rust_mitigation.strategy: Use #[repr(C)] with manual offset calculation or #[repr(C)] unions
rust_mitigation.implementation: Example: CERT_ALT_NAME_ENTRY uses union for pOtherName/pDirectoryName, implement as Rust union with #[repr(C)]
rust_mitigation.safety: All union field access is unsafe, provide safe wrapper functions that validate tag fields
rust_mitigation.testing: Add layout tests using std::mem::offset_of! macro to verify binary compatibility

tricky_patterns.challenge: C# pins byte arrays for P/Invoke, must free handle in finally block

rust_mitigation.strategy: Use Box::pin() or stack-allocated arrays for P/Invoke
rust_mitigation.implementation: For CERTTRANSBLOB: let data = Box::pin(bytes); let ptr = data.as_ptr(); pass ptr to FFI
rust_mitigation.safety: Pinned data must outlive FFI call, use lifetimes or RAII wrappers
rust_mitigation.pattern: Create struct BlobGuard { data: Pin<Box<[u8]>>, ptr: *const u8 } impl Drop

tricky_patterns.challenge: Dynamic COM object creation via ProgID strings like 'X509Enrollment.CX509PrivateKey'

rust_mitigation.strategy: Replace with static COM interface definitions in windows-rs
rust_mitigation.safety: Static typing is safer than reflection, compile-time interface verification
rust_mitigation.notes: ProgID was used for late binding, Rust uses early binding via interface definitions

rust_mitigation.implementation: Wrap in safe abstraction: struct RemoteRegistryKey { hkey: HKEY } impl Drop
rust_mitigation.safety: All registry operations are unsafe, validate paths, handle access denied errors

tricky_patterns.challenge: OpenProcessToken → DuplicateToken → ImpersonateLoggedOnUser with proper cleanup

rust_mitigation.strategy: RAII pattern with Drop trait for automatic RevertToSelf
rust_mitigation.implementation: struct TokenGuard { token: HANDLE } impl Drop { RevertToSelf() }
rust_mitigation.safety: All token operations are unsafe, validate process handle, ensure drop on panic (use scopeguard crate)
rust_mitigation.security: Document privilege requirements, log impersonation attempts, add audit trail

tricky_patterns.challenge: C# exceptions for error handling with finally blocks for cleanup

rust_mitigation.strategy: Result<T, E> with thiserror for error types, Drop trait for cleanup
rust_mitigation.implementation: Define enum CertifyError with variants for each error category (LdapError, ComError, CryptoError, etc.)
rust_mitigation.pattern: Use ? operator for propagation, implement From<T> for error conversions
rust_mitigation.finally_equivalent: Drop trait or scopeguard::defer! macro for cleanup

tricky_patterns.challenge: CryptEncodeObjectEx for ASN.1 DER encoding of X.509 extensions

rust_mitigation.strategy: Use der crate (DER encoding), x509-cert crate (X.509 structures)
rust_mitigation.implementation: Define ASN.1 structures with #[derive(Sequence)] from der_derive
rust_mitigation.safety: DER encoding is safe, but parsing requires validation of all input data
rust_mitigation.testing: Add round-trip tests (encode → decode → compare), test with known-good certificates

tricky_patterns.challenge: BouncyCastle used for PKCS#12 (PFX) export and PEM conversion

rust_mitigation.strategy: Use RustCrypto crates: rsa, x509-cert, pkcs8, pkcs12, pem
rust_mitigation.implementation: Replace Pkcs12Store with pkcs12 crate, use pem crate for PEM encoding
rust_mitigation.safety: RustCrypto crates are memory-safe, but crypto operations require careful key handling
rust_mitigation.notes: RustCrypto is well-maintained, audited, and widely used in Rust ecosystem

tricky_patterns.challenge: Manual NTLM handshake via AcquireCredentialsHandle, InitializeSecurityContext

rust_mitigation.strategy: Use windows-sys for secur32.dll bindings, or sspi crate for higher-level API
rust_mitigation.implementation: Define SecHandle, SecBuffer structures with #[repr(C)], implement NTLM client
rust_mitigation.safety: All SSPI calls are unsafe, validate buffer sizes, zero credential buffers on drop
rust_mitigation.alternative: Consider using reqwest crate with windows-auth feature for HTTP NTLM

migration_notes.disarmed_mode: C# has DISARMED build configuration (read-only). Rust port should support similar feature flag: --features disarmed
migration_notes.reflection_elimination: C# uses Type.GetTypeFromProgID() for COM objects. Rust uses static COM interfaces, no reflection needed
migration_notes.inheritance_to_composition: C# uses inheritance (CertificateAuthorityEnterprise : CertificateAuthority). Rust uses struct composition
migration_notes.exception_to_result: All C# exceptions converted to Result<T, CertifyError> with detailed error context
migration_notes.idisposable_to_drop: All C# IDisposable types use Drop trait in Rust for automatic cleanup
migration_notes.nullable_references: C# uses nullable reference types (string?). Rust uses Option<String>
migration_notes.async_consideration: C# is synchronous. Consider async/await for LDAP and HTTP operations in Rust for better concurrency

linux_support.enumeration: Partially supported (LDAP queries work, but no access to Windows-specific attributes)
linux_support.forge: Fully supported (pure crypto, no Windows APIs)
linux_support.recommendation: Provide clear error messages on Linux for Windows-only features
